notes: All scenarios share the TxQ model constants from postfiatd TxQ.h at commit 0085a1ff: base fee level 256, minimum escalation multiplier 128000 (= baseLevel * 500), queue capacity max(2000, 20 ledgers * target), max 10 queued transactions per account, LastLedgerSequence buffer 2 ledgers.

recovery_seconds is the adversary's key-recovery time in seconds: a parameter of the adversary-capability model, NOT a measured quantity. 30 s is the mature-CRQC tier; 3.5 s is the advanced-CRQC tier (one ledger close); 28800 s (8 h) is the near-term tier from the Lux threat model Table 1 (Ed25519 key recovery, ~2,310 logical qubits, 1 us T-gate time).
fee_premium 50.0: the adversary's competing transaction pays fifty times the victim's fee level.
last_ledger_window is the LastLedgerSequence window in ledgers from broadcast. The fee-policy scenario tightens it to 5 ledgers and raises the minimum fee level to 512 (2x base).

signature_scheme ed25519 means the adversary can recover keys (Shor-vulnerable). ml-dsa-65 means signatures are quantum-resistant, so recovery never completes and the hijack rate is 0 by construction.

commit_reveal true means each value transfer is a commit transaction (hash only, no public key, no value) followed by a reveal bound to the validated commit; a forged reveal cannot match the commit, so the hijack rate is 0 by construction.

scenarios.description: Normal load, 20 tx/s, Ed25519 signatures, mature-CRQC adversary (30 s recovery).
scenarios.name: baseline

scenarios.description: High load, 80 tx/s, Ed25519 signatures, mature-CRQC adversary (30 s recovery). Queue builds, exposure stretches past the recovery time.
scenarios.name: congested

scenarios.description: High load, 40 value-transfers/s (80 tx/s on-chain: commit + reveal per transfer), commit-reveal mitigation, mature-CRQC adversary (30 s recovery).
scenarios.name: congested-commit-reveal

scenarios.description: High load, 80 tx/s, fee/sequence-policy mitigation (LastLedgerSequence window 5 ledgers, minimum fee level 512), mature-CRQC adversary (30 s recovery).
scenarios.name: congested-fee-policy

scenarios.description: High load, 80 tx/s, ML-DSA-65 signatures (quantum-resistant), mature-CRQC adversary (30 s recovery). Recovery never completes.
scenarios.name: congested-ml-dsa

scenarios.description: Normal load, 20 tx/s, Ed25519 signatures, near-term adversary (8 h recovery, Lux Table 1 estimate). Control: recovery cannot complete inside any mempool exposure window.
scenarios.name: near-term-control

scenarios.description: High load, 80 tx/s, Ed25519 signatures, advanced-CRQC adversary (3.5 s recovery, one ledger close). Sensitivity case: recovery completes inside a single ledger.
scenarios.name: congested-fast-adversary
